- When sentiment turns negative in the recent history, reduce forecasted price momentum and avoid sharp upward moves.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive over recent days, model should not over-forecast downward moves; expect slight mean reversion toward prior range.  
- After a recent spike (e.g., >90), model tends to over-forecast subsequent prices — cap forecasted peaks at 10–15% below the spike peak.  
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often under-responds — adjust forecast to show a sharper decline or mean-reversion toward prior 10-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently underestimates early price drops (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is negative — increase initial forecast slightly above true outcome.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to over-smooth transitions — use a slight “jerk” or step adjustment in forecast to reflect sentiment volatility.
